claims.statement: HO-3 edition 2011-05 remains governing for policies written under it regardless of reporting date, while multistate HO-3 edition 2018-09 supersedes it for policies written on or after 2018-09-01; the later Coverage B changes must not be retroactively applied to a 2011-05 policy.

Under HO-3 2018-09 Section I B.1, Coverage B includes other structures on the defined residence premises that are separated by clear space or connected to the dwelling only by a fence, utility line, or similar connection; HO-3 2011-05 B.1 contains only the clear-space formulation.
Both HO-3 2011-05 B.2 and HO-3 2018-09 B.2 set Coverage B at 10% of the Coverage A limit as additional insurance.

HO-3 2018-09 B.3 does not cover an other structure rented or held for rental to a person who is not a tenant of the dwelling, unless it is used solely as a private garage; this B.3 limitation is absent from the supplied HO-3 2011-05 Coverage B text.

For HO-3 2018-09, Coverage B property is insured only against direct physical loss except as excluded by Section I, so meeting the structure scope and having a 10% limit does not by itself establish coverage.

The HO-3 2018-09 Section I water, earth-movement, neglect and deterioration, ordinance-or-law, and intentional-loss exclusions constrain Coverage B losses; the water exclusions A.1 through A.3 apply regardless of another contributing cause or event.

When HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 is attached, W.1 writes back the HO-3 A.3 sewer/drain and sump backup, overflow, or discharge exclusion for direct physical loss to Coverage B property, including an event resulting from equipment mechanical breakdown.

Under attached HO 04 90 edition 2010-10, the water-backup benefit has a $5,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless a higher limit is shown, is part of the Coverage B limit, uses a separate $500 deductible, retains the policy settlement basis for Coverage B, and is subject to its known-maintenance-failure condition.

Attached HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 provides limited Coverage B fungi, wet or dry rot, or bacteria coverage only when it results from a Section I insured peril during the policy period; it writes back HO-3 2018-09 C.2 only to that extent and leaves the identified underlying water and seepage exclusions operative.

The attached HO 04 81 edition 2018-09 fungi benefit is a $10,000 per-policy-period aggregate unless a higher limit is shown, is part of rather than additional to Coverage B, includes the specified removal and access costs, and separately requires mitigation of known or reasonably knowable water intrusion.

When HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 is attached, O.1 writes back HO-3 2018-09 D.1 only for increased cost actually incurred to repair, rebuild, or demolish a damaged other structure due to an ordinance or law in force at loss and only where the underlying Section I loss is covered; it is not a write-back for an otherwise excluded cause of loss.

The attached HO 04 16 edition 2018-09 ordinance-or-law benefit is additional insurance of 10% of Coverage A unless a higher percentage is shown and does not reduce Coverage B; it is payable only after damaged-property settlement, for costs actually incurred within its completion deadline and subject to its retained exclusions.

For HO-3 2018-09 Section I claims, the insured must give prompt notice, protect property from further damage, and submit a signed sworn proof of loss within 60 days after request; the declarations deductible applies to each Section I loss subject to the state-endorsed windstorm-or-hail rule.
HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 W.4 separately preserves the HO-3 A.1 exclusion for flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, storm surge, and overflow of a body of water.
HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 W.4 separately preserves the HO-3 A.2 exclusion for water below the surface of the ground.

HO 04 90 edition 2010-10 remains in force for policies written under it regardless of when loss is reported. Edition 2026-01 replaced it for policies written on or after 2026-01-01, and although 2027-01 supersedes 2026-01 for policies written on or after 2027-01-01, 2026-01 remains in force for policies written under it and governs their losses regardless of reporting date; the exact attached endorsement edition must therefore be identified before applying water-backup terms.

When HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 is attached to a compatible selected HO-3 policy, W.1 supplies the narrow direct-physical-loss write-back for the selected base form's A.3 sewer/drain-backup or sump-equipment overflow/discharge exclusion, including an event resulting from equipment mechanical breakdown.
HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.1 exclusion for flood, surface water, waves, tidal water, storm surge, and overflow of a body of water.
HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.4 separately preserves the selected HO-3 A.2 exclusion for water below the surface of the ground, including the specified pressure, seepage, and leakage routes.

For loss covered under attached HO 04 90 edition 2026-01, W.2 sets a $10,000 per-policy-period sublimit unless higher declared, within rather than additional to the A/B/C limits; W.3 applies a separate $1,000 deductible instead of the Section I deductible; and W.7 retains the attached policy's Coverage B settlement basis.

HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 retains the W.5 known-and-unremedied maintenance condition and adds W.6: if the residence premises has finished area below grade, endorsement coverage requires an installed and operable backwater valve or equivalent backflow-prevention device on the serving sewer line at the time of loss; W.6 did not appear in edition 2010-10.

Florida and Texas water-backup appetite guides are non-contractual underwriting guidance with battery-backed-sump-pump criteria at specified below-grade and higher-limit binding thresholds; those criteria do not establish, replace, or add the HO 04 90 edition 2026-01 W.6 backflow-prevention condition.

For an attached HO 04 90 2027-01, W.1 provides the narrow write-back to the selected HO-3 form's A.3 sewer/drain-backup or sump-event exclusion for stated direct physical loss to Coverage B property, including an event resulting from mechanical breakdown; it does not write back A.1 flood/surface-water or A.2 subsurface-water exclusions, which W.4 retains.

HO 04 90 2027-01 applies a $10,000 default policy-period sublimit within the applicable A/B/C limits, a separate $1,000 deductible instead of the Section I deductible, the same W.5 known-unremedied maintenance condition, and W.6's finished-below-grade backflow-prevention condition carried unchanged from 2026-01; Coverage B loss settlement remains on the basis stated in the attached policy under W.7.
